column1: If there's anything we can do to make your extended stay more comfy, you'll be sure to let us know, right?
column2: 如果我們有什麼能讓你這趟「長期住宿」過得更舒服，你會記得告訴我們的，對吧？

column1: You know, pigs can be kosher...it all depends on how you kill 'em.
column2: 你知道嗎，豬也可以宰得潔淨（kosher）……全看你怎麼宰的。

column1: Sure thing. Catch you later, Rabbi.
column2: 沒問題。回頭見了，拉比。

column1: Comfortable?
column2: 舒服嗎？

column1: I'd be a lot more comfortable with a .22 slug buried in your...
column2: 要是有顆 .22 子彈埋在你的……我會舒服得多。

column1: Temper, temper.
column2: 消消氣，消消氣。

column1: I've got a little surprise for you.
column2: 我有個小驚喜要給你。

column1: What, you learned to chew gum and walk at the same time? Yippee skippee.
column2: 怎麼，你學會邊嚼口香糖邊走路了？哇，真了不起。

column1: Sorry, Taselli, I can't hear you. The violins are playing too loudly.
column2: 抱歉了，Taselli，我聽不到你在說什麼。小提琴的聲音太大聲了。

column1: Cram it!
column2: 閉嘴啦！

column1: Move your can into the cell, Mr. Hoffman. I think you know the way.
column2: 把你的屁股移進牢房裡，Hoffman 先生。我想你知道路怎麼走。

column1: Please walk to the center of the room.
column2: 請走到房間中央。

column1: Stand against the wall and don't move.
column2: 站到牆邊，不要動。

column1: I'll be outta here in 15 minutes, and I'm comin' after you. So kiss your ass goodbye.
column2: 我十五分鐘後就會離開這裡，然後我要找你算帳。你就等著跟自己的小命說再見吧。

column1: Don't bet on it, pig.
column2: 我勸你別打這個賭，豬頭。

column1: I'll take care of this. Don't you have some paperwork to do, Paul?
column2: 這裡交給我處理就好。你不是還有文件要處理嗎，Paul？

column1: You look good in matching bracelets.
column2: 你戴著這對「手鐲」還挺好看的。

column1: I got a match for you, pigman.
column2: 我這裡也有一副要給你的，豬頭。

column1: Can it, punk!
column2: 閉嘴，小混混！

column1: Oh, one more thing.
column2: 噢，還有一件事。

column1: Jack seems to be quite amused. Perhaps he just enjoys his own company.
column2: Jack 看起來相當開心。也許他只是很享受自己一個人的樂趣。

column1: They're a fine pair, aren't they?
column2: 他們倆真是絕配，不是嗎？

column1: Pretty pathetic centerpiece for any room, eh?
column2: 當任何房間的擺飾，都挺可悲的吧？

column1: You think she might be willing but the atmosphere in this prison is a little too much like a cheap Linda Blair movie. Someplace more romantic would be better.
column2: 你覺得她似乎有點意願，但這座監獄的氣氛太像廉價版的 Linda Blair 電影了。換個更浪漫的地方應該比較好。

column1: Wanna help?
column2: 要幫忙嗎？

column1: You're puzzled by a strange, warm and fuzzy sensation after your conversation with Marie. Easy, boy. You've got to concentrate on the business at hand. Anything less than 100 percent can prove fatal.
column2: 跟 Marie 聊完後，你被一股奇怪、溫暖又酥麻的感覺搞得一頭霧水。冷靜點，小子。你得專心處理眼前的事，稍有分心都可能致命。

column1: Geez, Sonny. Do I have to see that ugly mug all day?
column2: 天啊，Sonny。我一整天都得看著你那張醜臉嗎？

column1: Just keep away from mirrors, Paul.
column2: Paul，你就離鏡子遠一點吧。

column1: So where's the prisoner I'm supposed to visit?
column2: 那我要探視的犯人在哪裡？

column1: She's in one of the cells. I hear she's an old flame of yours. So, have you and her performed nature's mystery dance?
column2: 她在其中一間牢房裡。聽說她是你的舊情人。所以呢，你們倆跳過「大自然的神祕之舞」了嗎？

column1: Well, you just think about it on one of your lonely Saturday nights, Paul. Thanks for all the great info.
column2: 好啦，Paul，你就留著在某個孤單的星期六晚上慢慢想吧。謝謝你提供的這些寶貴情報。

column1: That guy proves that evolution hasn't been 100-percent effective.
column2: 這傢伙證明了演化並沒有百分之百成功。

column1: Paul looks like the kind of guy built to wear leisure suits and spend his life in cheesy discos. His orange tan suggests an unfortunate go-round with a tube of Instant-Tan. All he needs are a few gold chains and a bottle of breath spray.
column2: Paul 看起來就是那種天生適合穿休閒西裝、把一生耗在俗氣迪斯可舞廳的人。他那身橘得不自然的膚色，八成是跟一瓶速效古銅乳液纏鬥的悲慘結果。他只差幾條金項鍊和一瓶口氣清新噴霧了。

column1: Hey, Sonny-boy! Sounds like Marie's warm for your form! Gonna get a little free...
column2: 嘿，Sonny 小子！聽起來 Marie 對你的身材挺有意思的嘛！看樣子要來點免費的……

column1: Paul, I swear, one of these days, you're going to open your mouth a little too wide, and you're going to force me to jam my fist into it.
column2: Paul，我發誓，總有一天你那張嘴會張得太大，逼得我不得不把拳頭塞進去。

column1: There's an uncomfortable silence.
column2: 現場出現一陣尷尬的沉默。

column1: Sorry, Sonny.
column2: 抱歉，Sonny。

column1: Hey, Sonny, how's it going?
column2: 嘿，Sonny，最近好嗎？

column1: How ya doin', Paul.
column2: 你好嗎，Paul。

column1: Fine, thanks.
column2: 還不錯，謝了。

column1: Paul, I've got a couple more cell-stuffers for you.
column2: Paul，我這裡還有幾個要塞進牢房的傢伙給你。

column1: I've got another guest for your fine establishment, Paul.
column2: Paul，我又給你這間「高級旅館」帶來一位貴賓了。

column1: He looks well-lubed. He better not spackle my cell, Bonds. You're cleaning it up if he does. What's the official violation?
column2: 他看起來喝得很茫。他最好別把我的牢房弄得一團糟，Bonds。要是他吐了，你自己負責清。他的正式罪名是什麼？

column1: Paul, we've got another winner. Tell 'em what he's won.
column2: Paul，我們又抓到一位「幸運兒」。告訴他，他贏得了什麼獎。

column1: Ooh, this one's lucky, Sonny, he gets a copy of our home game to play and enjoy right in his very own home. Hah!
column2: 噢，這位運氣真好，Sonny，他可以把我們的「居家版遊戲」帶回自己家裡慢慢玩。哈！

column1: Here you go.
column2: 給你。

column1: Well, well! Good thing you got this here when you did, Bonds. Hold on, I'll process it.
column2: 哎呀哎呀！還好你及時把這個帶來了，Bonds。等一下，我來處理。

column1: Thanks, Bonds. He's all checked in...but he ain't checkin' out.
column2: 謝了，Bonds。他已經「入住」登記完畢……但他可退不了房。

column1: Got something for ya, Paul.
column2: 有東西要給你，Paul。

column1: Don't keep me in suspense, Bonds. Let's have it.
column2: 別吊我胃口了，Bonds。拿出來吧。

column1: Assault and battery, eh? Well, let's just book him for assault this time, and tell 'em battery's not included. Har!
column2: 傷害罪加上毆打罪，嗯？這次我們就先建檔收押傷害罪，跟他說毆打不算在內好了。哈！

column1: Burglary? Tsk, tsk. Don't he know that good always triumphs over evil?
column2: 竊盜罪？嘖嘖。他難道不知道邪不勝正這句話嗎？

column1: Driver's license not in possession, eh? Don't tell me. He left it in his other pants, right?
column2: 沒帶駕照在身上，嗯？別跟我說，他一定是放在另一件褲子裡了，對吧？

column1: Okay, we're booking one for driving with a suspended license.
column2: 好，這位是吊扣駕照期間開車，建檔收押。

column1: Hit-and-run, eh? My mother was killed by a hit-and-run. Let's hope this guy doesn't give me a hard time.
column2: 肇事逃逸，嗯？我母親就是被肇事逃逸的車撞死的。希望這傢伙別給我惹麻煩。

column1: Driving too slow in the fast lane, eh? Gee, what do we give him for that...one month or two?
column2: 在快車道上龜速行駛，嗯？天啊，這種罪該判他多久……一個月還是兩個月？

column1: Following too close, huh? Better watch out for this one in the shower.
column2: 跟車跟太近，嗯？這傢伙進去洗澡時最好小心點。

column1: Exceeding the maximum speed limit. Another speed freak.
column2: 超過最高速限。又一個飆車狂。

column1: Not in full control of his faculties, huh? Boy, you bringin' all of Congress in here?
column2: 神智不清，嗯？老兄，你是打算把整個國會議員都抓進來喔？

column1: The booking room is decorated in that oh-so-fashionable gut-boggling institutional green.
column2: 這間收押登記室，裝潢成那種令人反胃的「時髦」機關綠。

column1: Hey, keep your grubby fingers offa the glass, Bonds.
column2: 嘿，Bonds，你那雙髒手別碰玻璃。

column1: A heavy bulletproof window separates Paul from the clientele. It's best that way. His breath could easily be ruled a violation of one's civil rights.
column2: 一片厚重的防彈玻璃把 Paul 跟他的「客戶」隔開來。這樣最好，因為他的口氣搞不好會被判定是侵犯人權。

column1: Don't sit out here, Bonds. You're being anti-social.
column2: 別坐在外面，Bonds。你這樣太不合群了。

column1: It's a bench.
column2: 這是一張長椅。

column1: Don't do that, you'll get a splinter.
column2: 別這麼做，你會被木刺扎到的。

column1: You admire the wooden decking, trying not to notice the ancient chunks of food stuck between the planks.
column2: 你欣賞著這片木製地板，努力不去注意木板縫裡卡著的陳年食物殘渣。

column1: Leave the flowers alone. They get enough trouble from the neighborhood dogs.
column2: 別去碰那些花。牠們光是應付附近的狗就已經夠麻煩了。

column1: The flowers smell wonderful, don't they?
column2: 這些花聞起來很香，對吧？

column1: The flowers have only the simplest of nervous systems; they do not respond in any measurable fashion.
column2: 這些花只有最簡單的神經系統，不會有任何可觀察到的反應。

column1: The fern's leaves are light and airy.
column2: 這株蕨類的葉子輕盈飄逸。

column1: An attractive fern hangs outside the Blue Room door.
column2: 一盆漂亮的蕨類植物掛在 Blue Room 門外。

column1: The ferns are too busy enjoying the fresh air and sunshine to bother replying.
column2: 這些蕨類正忙著享受新鮮空氣和陽光，懶得理你。

column1: You can go shopping some other time, Bonds.
column2: Bonds，你可以改天再去逛街。

column1: The Blue Room is nestled between many charming little shops.
column2: Blue Room 座落在幾間迷人的小店之間。

column1: There's nothing on the ground that requires your attention.
column2: 地上沒有什麼值得你注意的東西。

column1: It's the parking lot.
column2: 這是停車場。

column1: Quit teasing the foliage.
column2: 別再逗弄那些植物了。

column1: Nice plants. You remember that plants are supposed to clean up the atmosphere. You briefly wish they'd help clean up the neighborhood... No, Bonds. No carnivorous plants. Play Space Quest II for that.
column2: 不錯的植物。你記得植物應該有淨化空氣的功能。你一時興起，希望它們也能順便清一清這附近的治安……不行，Bonds。這裡沒有食人植物。想玩這套，去玩 Space Quest II 吧。

column1: The plants ignore your clumsy attempt at communication.
column2: 這些植物無視了你笨拙的溝通嘗試。

column1: That's a little too big for your rock collection, Bonds.
column2: Bonds，這對你的石頭收藏來說有點太大了。

column1: It's a rock.
column2: 這是一顆石頭。

column1: It's bad enough that you talk to plants. Get a grip, Bonds.
column2: 你會跟植物講話已經夠糟了。振作一點，Bonds。

column1: You're outside the Blue Room, a popular hangout for cops.
column2: 你在 Blue Room 外面，這裡是警察們愛去的熱門去處。

column1: Don't take the sign. It's useful right where it is.
column2: 別把招牌拿走。它擺在原位才有用。

column1: The sign for the Blue Room was hand-painted by the owner's daughter.
column2: Blue Room 的招牌是老闆的女兒親手畫的。

column1: You'd better see Jack first.
column2: 你最好先去見 Jack。

column1: Leave the sign alone. It's fine where it is.
column2: 別動那塊招牌。它放在那裡就很好。

column1: The sign says: Soup of the Day--Moulder Stew.
column2: 招牌上寫著：今日例湯——發霉燉肉。

column1: Spotting the sediment of cola and ketchup on the table, you withdraw your hand.
column2: 你注意到桌上有可樂和番茄醬的殘渣，於是把手縮了回來。

column1: Charming white plastic lawn furniture.
column2: 迷人的白色塑膠庭院家具。

column1: Good for you. Everyone should hug a tree from time to time.
column2: 很好。每個人偶爾都該抱抱樹。

column1: This tree was donated by the Lytton Police force to the town of Lytton three years ago.
column2: 這棵樹是三年前 Lytton 警察局捐贈給 Lytton 鎮的。

column1: The tree seems glad to see you.
column2: 這棵樹似乎很高興見到你。

column1: Don't get too close, Bonds. That little piece of Americana could drop on you like a collection agent.
column2: 別靠太近，Bonds。這個小小的美式風情擺設，可能會像討債公司一樣突然砸到你頭上。

column1: It's one of those big umbrellas that leaks in the rain, cracks in the sun, and blows over in the slightest breeze.
column2: 這是那種下雨會漏水、曬太陽會龜裂、風一吹就倒的大陽傘。

column1: Bobby will be happy to serve you.
column2: Bobby 會很樂意為你服務。

column1: Back there is where Bobby, your bartender, keeps all his deadly hangover generators.
column2: 你的酒保 Bobby 把他那些「致命宿醉製造機」都放在那後面。

column1: You can't reach it, Bonds. Besides, you already picked up all the bad artwork you need at the Starving Artists Sale at the local Happyday Inn.
column2: 你搆不到它，Bonds。而且你已經在當地 Happyday Inn 的「窮藝術家特賣會」上，買夠了你需要的爛畫。

column1: It's an all-American crushed-velvet Nude Lady Behind the Bar painting.
column2: 這是一幅道地美式風格的絨布裸女酒吧畫。

column1: Some seedy citizens rest at the bar.
column2: 幾個看起來不太正經的傢伙在吧台邊休息。

column1: Don't grab Bobby. He's got a quick temper.
column2: 別去抓 Bobby。他脾氣很衝。

column1: That's Bobby Gomez. He retired from the force a few years back when this fine establishment became available. He got out of police work and into something he felt was much safer: operating a bar.
column2: 那是 Bobby Gomez。幾年前這間「高級場所」剛好要頂讓，他就從警局退休了。他離開了警察工作，轉行做他認為安全多了的事——開酒吧。

column1: Hi, Sonny. Nice to see you.
column2: 嗨，Sonny。很高興見到你。

column1: Don't worry, Sonny, he'll be alright.
column2: 別擔心，Sonny，他不會有事的。

column1: Later, Sonny.
column2: 回頭見，Sonny。

column1: Don't touch that bar, Bonds. You don't know where it's been.
column2: 別碰那個吧台，Bonds。你不知道它經歷過什麼。

column1: Across this bar has passed nearly an ocean of ales and other alcohol-laden attitude adjusters.
column2: 這座吧台上，流過的啤酒和各種「調整心情」的酒精飲料，多得快能匯成一片海洋了。

column1: It's a booth.
column2: 這是一個卡座。

column1: On closer inspection, you discover the words "Robin of Locksley was here" carved into the wood. Damn vandals.
column2: 你仔細一看，發現木頭上刻著「Robin of Locksley was here」的字樣。這些該死的破壞公物的傢伙。

column1: What were you thinking of doing, walking off with it?
column2: 你到底在打什麼主意，想把它整個扛走嗎？

column1: It's the universal symbol of masculinity, the Bullcinch. Just looking at its wrought-iron curves and angles makes your testosterone levels rise.
column2: 這是象徵陽剛之氣的萬用圖騰——Bullcinch。光是看著它那鍛鐵打造的曲線和稜角，就讓你的睪固酮濃度直線上升。

column1: You sneak a fingerful of icing for the road.
column2: 你偷偷用手指挖了一坨糖霜，準備路上吃。

column1: It sure looks good. Too bad there was nobody to jump out of it.
column2: 看起來真不錯。可惜沒人從裡面跳出來。

column1: Functional chairs. Not as nice as the ones in Lt. Morgan's office, but they'll do.
column2: 中規中矩的椅子。沒有 Morgan 中尉辦公室裡的那麼氣派，但堪用。

column1: You sit down with Jack. It's nice to have a few minutes to talk with him before the party, you think to yourself.
column2: 你在 Jack 身邊坐下。你心想，能在派對開始前跟他聊個幾分鐘也不錯。

column1: You're cute, Sonny, but if you do that again, I'll break your fingers.
column2: 你是滿可愛的，Sonny，但你要是再這樣，我就打斷你的手指。

column1: This is Clarice. She has been working here for as long as you can remember.
column2: 這位是 Clarice。從你有記憶以來，她就一直在這裡工作。

column1: Have a good one, Sonny.
column2: 祝你順利，Sonny。

column1: Face-down on the floor is not a good position for an officer of the law to be in, Bonds.
column2: Bonds，臉朝下趴在地上，對一名執法人員來說可不是什麼好姿勢。

column1: The floor is relatively clean for an establishment of this calibre.
column2: 以這種等級的場所來說，地板算是相當乾淨了。

column1: You give Jack a friendly pat on the shoulder.
column2: 你友善地拍了拍 Jack 的肩膀。

column1: You gently tap Jack on the shoulder.
column2: 你輕輕拍了拍 Jack 的肩膀。

column1: It's your old friend, Jack Cobb.
column2: 是你的老朋友，Jack Cobb。

column1: Oh, there's Jack.
column2: 噢，Jack 在那裡。

column1: Hey, Jack! Happy birthday, man.
column2: 嘿，Jack！生日快樂，老兄。

column1: Huh? Oh, thanks, Sonny.
column2: 嗯？噢，謝了，Sonny。

column1: You are suddenly certain that Jack is lying, and that scares you.
column2: 你突然確信 Jack 在說謊，這讓你感到不安。

column1: I don't know for sure. But she's been so nasty for the past few months. Secretive. I know, all teenagers are like that. But her grades are slipping.
column2: 我也說不準。但這幾個月她變得很難搞，鬼鬼祟祟的。我知道，青少年都這樣。但她的成績一直在退步。
